## About Me

I am a PhD candidate in Economics at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, expected to graduate in May 2027. I am on the **2026–27 academic job market**.

My research lies at the intersection of **environmental, urban, and spatial economics**. I study how environmental risks and natural disasters affect housing markets, households, and local economic outcomes.

My research uses spatial, administrative, environmental, economic, weather, and nighttime-lights data to examine the economic effects of environmental risks and shocks.

I also have experience in applied economic policy research through my work as a Short-Term Consultant with the **World Bank's Macroeconomics, Trade & Investment Global Practice** in the Nepal Country Office.

## Research Interests

Environmental Economics · Urban Economics · Spatial Economics · Applied Microeconomics

## Job Market Paper

**Water Contamination and Real Estate Prices: Evidence from Hawaii's Red Hill Fuel Leak**

My job market paper examines how information about environmental contamination risk affects housing markets. Using spatially detailed property transactions and environmental monitoring data, I study how housing prices respond to changes in perceived environmental risk.
